title: Quantum-Enhanced Computational Fluid Dynamics: Hybrid Quantum–Classical Solvers for High-Fidelity Simulation of Turbulence and Multiphase Flow in Mechanical System Design
abstract: Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) plays a central role in mechanical system design by enabling the simulation of complex flow phenomena such as turbulence, phase transitions, and fluid–structure interactions. However, high-fidelity CFD simulations—particularly those involving turbulent and multiphase flows—are often limited by the computational cost of solving large-scale, nonlinear, and high-dimensional systems of equations. This study explores the potential of quantum-enhanced computational fluid dynamics, focusing on hybrid quantum–classical solvers as a next-generation approach to overcoming these limitations. By integrating quantum algorithms with classical numerical methods, hybrid frameworks aim to accelerate key CFD tasks such as linear system solving, optimization, and high-dimensional state exploration while preserving the stability and accuracy of established solvers. The paper examines how quantum principles such as superposition and entanglement can be leveraged to improve convergence rates and design-space exploration in turbulence modeling and multiphase flow simulations. Through a conceptual and methodological analysis, this work highlights the opportunities, current constraints, and future implications of quantum-enhanced CFD for mechanical system design, offering a forward-looking perspective on the convergence of quantum computing and fluid mechanics.

title: AIAO : AI Agent Ontology *v1
abstract: Agentic AI systems, computational entities that perceive, reason, and act with varying degrees of autonomy, are rapidly proliferating across digital, physical, and socio technical environments. Despite decades of research in intelligent agents, multi-agent systems, cognitive architectures, and human AI interaction, there is no widely adopted cross-domain semantic framework that supports consistent description, comparison, and interoperability of agentic systems. This paper introduces an ontology for Agentic AI designed as a unifying semantic layer across these traditions. The ontology is structured along six primary dimensions: autonomy level, functional role, embodiment, cognitive capability, interaction style, and operational scope. Across these dimensions, it defines 25 core agent classes and aligns them with relevant web and semantic standards, including RDF, OWL, SPARQL, and related interoperability technologies. Rather than proposing entirely new categories, the framework synthesizes established classification schemes from the literature and organizes them within a multi-dimensional model suitable for formal representation. We describe the literature analysis, design methodology, ontology structure, and evaluation criteria, and provide machine-readable artifacts in both JSON Schema and OWL to support reuse, extension, and integration with knowledge graphs and web-based systems. The ontology is positioned as shared semantic infrastructure intended to reduce conceptual fragmentation, support interoperability, and facilitate the development of open, evolvable ecosystems of agentic AI systems.

title: MAD-OGRE: A Multi-Agent Debate Framework for Open Geographic Entity Relation Extraction Based on Large Language Models
abstract: # MAD-OGRE: A Multi-Agent Debate Framework for Open Geographic Entity Relation Extraction Based on Large Language Models ## 🧩 Core Logic The core code of this project is located in the `src/` directory, adopting a design pattern that separates **Roles** and **Actions**: ### 1. Core Modules * **`src/role/`**: Defines agent attributes, Prompt templates, and interaction logic. * **`src/action/`**: Implements specific business logic, API calls, and data processing. ### 2. Four Structural Patterns To address the complexity of geographic text, four parallel processing modules are designed: * **Independent Parallel**: Handles simple sentences or coordinate sentences with independent semantics. * **Progressive**: Handles complex sentences involving causality, chronological order, or hierarchical reasoning. * **One-to-Many**: Handles relationships where one head entity corresponds to multiple tail entities. * **Many-to-One**: Handles aggregate relationships where multiple head entities point to the same tail entity. ### 3. Multi-Agent Debate Pipeline Each structure contains a complete closed-loop debate process. Overview of the core workflow: 1. **Basic Extraction**: Entity recognition and preliminary relation extraction. 2. **Debate Optimization**: * Advisory Component (`_Three_advice`): Generates diverse evaluation viewpoints; * Core Debate (`_Debate`): Conducts multi-round interactions; * Decision Module (`_Decide`): Determines and outputs the final result. > Note: Since the core framework process is highly consistent across different sentence patterns, `###` is used below as a placeholder for the sentence pattern to illustrate the structure. Agent Role Definitions (Implementation Files) * `src/role/conventional_template/Extract_entityer.py`: General Entity Extraction Agent * `src/role/###/###_Cleaning.py`: Cleaning Agent * `src/role/###/###_Extract_Relationer.py`: Relation Extraction & Triple Generation Agent * `src/role/###/###_ThreeAdvicer.py`: Evaluation Opinion Generation (Advisor) Agent * `src/role/###/###_Debator.py`: Debate Agent * `src/role/###/###_Decider.py`: Decision Agent * `src/role/###/###_Summarizer.py`: Summarization & Correction Agent Agent Actions (Corresponding Implementations) * `src/action/conventional/Extract_entity.py`: General Entity Extraction Action * `src/action/###/###_Clean.py`: Cleaning Action * `src/action/###/###_Extract_Relationship.py`: Relation Extraction & Triple Generation Action * `src/action/###/###_Three_advice.py`: Evaluation Opinion Generation Action * `src/action/###/###_Debate.py`: Debate Action * `src/action/###/###_Decide.py`: Decision Action * `src/action/###/###_Summarize.py`: Summarization & Correction Action ## ⚙️ Experimental Setup To ensure the reproducibility of experiments, the default parameters used in the paper are as follows (unless overridden in specific experiment scripts): ### Triple Extraction Experiment Parameters | Parameter | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | **Model Version** | `Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct` | The model version used in the main experiments of the paper | | **Temperature** | `0.0` | Set to 0 to ensure determinism and consistency of results | | **Top_p** | `1.0` | Nucleus sampling parameter | | **Max Tokens** | `8192` | Maximum output length limit | | **Debate Rounds** | `3` | Default debate rounds (varies in Debate Rounds experiments) | > **Note:** The LLM parameters mentioned above are mainly managed in `config/`, while the number of debate rounds is controlled by the `DEBATE_ROUNDS` variable in different experiments. ### LLM Parameters for Experimental Result Evaluation | Parameter | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | **Model Version** | `Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct` | The model version used in the main experiments of the paper | | **Temperature** | `0.7` | Set to 0.7, as recommended by Qwen official documentation | | **Top_p** | `0.8` | Nucleus sampling parameter, recommended by Qwen official | | **Max Tokens** | `8192` | Maximum output length limit | | **presence_penalty** | `1.5` | Recommended by Qwen official | | **top_k** | `20` | Recommended by Qwen official | ### LLM Parameters in Comparison of Reasoning Capabilities: GRE vs. Open GRE Experiment | Parameter | Value | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | **Model Version** | `Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct` | The model version used in the main experiments of the paper | | **Temperature** | `0.0` | Set to 0 to ensure determinism and consistency of results | | **Top_p** | `1.0` | Nucleus sampling parameter | | **Max Tokens** | `8192` | Maximum output length limit | ## 🛠️ Installation This project supports modern Python environment management. Using `uv` is recommended for faster installation speed. ### Prerequisites * Python 3.11 or higher * An OpenAI-compatible API Key * Configured `uv` environment Since the project includes `uv.lock`, strict environment synchronization can be performed: ```bash uv sync ``` ### 🔑 Configuration Before running experiments, LLM settings must be configured according to the `metagpt` package requirements. 1. Create a `config` folder in the project root directory. 2. Create a `config2.yaml` file inside `config/`. 3. Copy the following content and fill in your actual information: ```yaml # config/config2.yaml llm: api_type: 'openai' # Optional: openai, azure, ollama, etc. api_key: 'sk-...' # Replace with your actual API Key model: 'Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct' # Recommended: Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct base_url: '...' # Optional: Custom endpoint URL # ...... # See metagpt official site for other configurations ``` ## 📊 Data Preparation and Format ### Dataset Description * **`data/CE-GRE-Eval/`**: Self-constructed OpenGRE dataset, containing geomorphic entities, processes, and causal relationships. * Core Modules * **`src/role/`**: Defines agent attributes, Prompt templates, and interaction logic. * **`src/action/`**: Implements specific business logic, API calls, and data processing. ### 2. title: A Scoping Analysis of Literature on the Enhancement of Security in Financial Message Systems.
abstract: The security of financial messaging systems is critical to safeguarding sensitive information and maintaining user trust in digital financial platforms. Despite advances in cryptographic techniques, existing systems remain vulnerable to channel-based and cryptographic attacks, including eavesdropping, tampering, and unauthorized access. Hybrid cryptographic models combining asymmetric and symmetric encryption have emerged as promising solutions to enhance confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity in message transmission. This scoping review systematically examines literature published between 2015 and 2025 to map current knowledge on user vulnerabilities in financial messaging systems and the role of hybrid cryptographic models in mitigating these risks. Guided by the PRISMA-ScR framework, 44 relevant studies were identified from nine scholarly databases and supplementary sources.

title: Learning Engineering by Design: An Agentic AI Application for Rapid, Personalized Health & Safety Training in Disaster Response and Hazardous Environments
abstract: Disaster response and hazardous materials (HAZMAT) cleanup require rapid preparation of diverse, transient workers for site-specific risks. Traditional methods fail to meet tight timelines, creating safety gaps. The Health & Safety Training (HST) Copilot, funded by NIEHS SBIR Phase I (Award 1R43ES037510-01), applies learning engineering principles to embed evidence-based design in an AI platform. Integrating ICICLE best practices and IEEE TLA frameworks, an 11-agent architecture generates personalized primers and assessments from site documents. Development follows a nested learning engineering cycle: human expertise assembly, agentic AI simulation, evidence/decision tracking (LEED-inspired), and refinement. Phase I SME rubric evaluation confirmed technical feasibility, instructional quality, and rapid generation, with stakeholder commitment to Phase II. Future studies will assess learning transfer and safety outcomes.

title: Role of Quantum Computing in India's Cybersecurity Ecosystem
abstract: Quantum computing is being seen as a disrupting factor with immense power to redefine the landscape of information cyberspace security. For India, as a large emerging nation with ever-increasing growth rates in digital technologies and initiatives like UPI, Aadhar-based identity and payment systems, 5G technologies, smart cities, and defense technologies, quantum computing provides risks and opportunities. Classical cryptographic technologies like RSA and ECC are transitioning towards obsolescence with the emergence of Shor’s Algorithm. Quantum computing offers prospects of a good alternative with quantum-safe technologies. This paper proposes a Quantum Cybersecurity Transition Framework (QCTF) for India as a way of adapting quantum computing for its information cyberspace. With the help of this framework and case studies, this paper shows how quantum computing can provide India with an information cyberspace security advantage. The results of this study emphasize and advocate for the incorporation and realization of quantum computing and quantum-safe technologies for information cyberspace security.

title: Perfiles del odio religioso en las redes sociales
abstract: This report is the result of the HatemediaReligion project (PC-24-0050), funded by the Fundación Pluralismo y Convivencia and implemented by Hatemedia, through the Universidad Internacional de La Rioja. What you are reading is not an exhaustive list of offensive messages nor a legal classification of hate speech. The aim of this text is to contribute to the understanding of its forms of production and persistence, with special attention to the religious sphere and from an applied, evidence-based perspective. Throughout this report, the focus deliberately shifts from the individual message to the body of messages and, from there, to the profiles that repeatedly issue them. In this way, isolated cases are distinguished from recurring patterns, and the moments when hostility takes center stage are identified.

title: AMorph: An End-to-End Morpheme Level Natural Language Processing Pipeline for Amharic
abstract: Morphological segmentation is foundational for Natural Language Processing in morphologically rich languages, such as Amharic, yet progress is constrained by limited gold annotations and fragmented toolchains.We present an end-toend framework that jointly addresses data creation and modeling for Amharic segmentation, part-of-speech tagging, and dependency parsing.Our approach begins with a silver-data generation pipeline that bootstraps segmentation labels from a rule-based analyzer and refines them through automated review, large language model assisted verification, and human-in-the-loop correction.Using the resulting supervision, we train an XLM-RoBERTa segmenter with a connectionist temporal classification (CTC) based character transduction objective, enabling reliable morpheme boundary prediction without explicit character-morpheme alignment.We then introduce a unified multi-task toolkit model that replaces the common practice of training separate systems per task.A shared pretrained encoder is jointly optimized for POS tagging and dependency parsing to better capture cross-task linguistic regularities while remaining parameter-efficient.The observed morpheme segmentation, POS tagging, and dependency parsing results support the conclusion that analyzer-bootstrapped supervision combined with multilingual pretrained encoders is effective for Amharic morphosyntactic modeling in low-resource settings.We release an open-source toolkit with simple APIs and an interactive visualization interface, enabling users to run the pipeline and inspect intermediate and final outputs for practical Amharic NLP development.API, documentation, and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/Netela-lab/AMorph.

title: On Left Adjoints Preserving Colimits in HoTT
abstract: We examine how the standard proof that left adjoints preserve colimits behaves in the setting of wild categories, a natural setting for synthetic homotopy theory inside homotopy type theory. We prove that the proof may fail for adjunctions between wild categories. Our core contribution, however, is a sufficient condition on the left adjoint for the proof to go through. The condition, called 2-coherence, expresses that the naturality structure of the hom-isomorphism commutes with composition of morphisms. We present two useful examples of this condition in action. First, we use it, along with a new version of a known trick for homogeneous types, to show that the suspension functor preserves graph-indexed colimits. Second, we show that every modality, viewed as a functor on coslices of a type universe, is 2-coherent as a left adjoint to the forgetful functor from the subcategory of modal types, thereby proving this subcategory is cocomplete. We have formalized our main results in Agda.

title: A Survey of Six Classical Classifiers, Including Algorithms, Methodological Characteristics, Foundational Variants, and Recent Advances
abstract: Classification is a core supervised learning task in data analysis, and six classical classifier families (k-Nearest Neighbors, Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Naïve Bayes) remain widely used in practice and underpin many subsequent variants. Although both single-family and multi-classifier surveys exist, there is still a gap for a method-centered study that, within a coherent framework, combines algorithmic representations for training and prediction, methodological characteristics, an explicit methodological comparison of the foundational variants within each family, and method-oriented advances published between 2020 and 2025. The survey is organized around a fixed set of performance-related perspectives, including accuracy, hyperparameter tuning, scalability, class imbalance, behavior in high-dimensional settings, decision-boundary complexity, interpretability, computational efficiency, and multiclass handling. It highlights strengths, weaknesses, and trade-offs across the six families and their variants, helping researchers and practitioners select or extend classification approaches. It also outlines future research directions arising from the limitations across the examined methods.

title: Scaling Analysis of Quantum Amplitude Estimation for Tokenized Asset Option Pricing: Validation and Barriers to Practical Advantage
abstract: We present an implementation and empirical validation of Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) for pricing European options on tokenized blockchain securities. Classical Monte Carlo (MC) methods require O(1/ε 2) samples to achieve pricing error ε, whereas QAE provides a quadratic asymptotic improvement with O(1/ε) query complexity. By benchmarking across discretization levels of 3-6 qubits (8-64 price bins), we empirically confirm the predicted O(1/ε) scaling under idealized simulation conditions. Our approach operates within near-term Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) constraints (9-10 qubits, ∼250 gate depth) and constitutes an end-to-end demonstration of quantum option pricing for tokenized assets. Experiments on Bitcoin and Ethereum derivatives show discretization error scaling as 1/ √ n bins , consistent with theory. We emphasize that this work validates theoretical scaling rather than practical advantage: discretization errors remain large at feasible qubit counts, state preparation costs are excluded, and current accuracy is insufficient for production use. We identify discretization as the primary bottleneck and estimate that 3-5 years of hardware advances are required for practical relevance.

title: Algorithmic approaches to detecting, mitigating, and defending against online misogyny: a scoping review
abstract: Online misogyny remains a persistent and evolving problem across social media and digital platforms, manifesting through hate speech, harassment, and gender-based abuse. While early research has focused primarily on the automated detection of misogynistic content, there is growing recognition that algorithmic systems also play a role in mitigation, moderation, counter-speech, and broader defensive responses. Following consultation with external stakeholders, including practitioners and researchers working in violence prevention and digital governance, it became clear that a detection-only focus did not adequately capture the full range of algorithmic interventions currently being developed and deployed. In response, this scoping review broadens the analytical lens to examine how algorithmic methods are used not only to identify online misogyny, but also to mitigate its impacts and support defensive or preventative strategies across platforms. In line with open science principles, this review has been registered separately from a previously registered scoping review protocol, with explicit linkage maintained between the two registrations.

title: "The Theory of Stochastic Stagnation
abstract: I introduce the Theory of Stochastic Stagnation to address a critical flaw in current AI trajectories: the transition from open-ended evolution to refined repetition. My research argues that by prioritizing error minimization, artificial systems systematically prune the 'tails' of probability distributions—the very regions where genuine novelty and innovation originate. This paper synthesizes empirical evidence from 2024-2025 to validate four core observations: the narrowing performance gap among top-tier models (shrinking from 11.9% to 5.4%) , the saturation of synthetic data on the web , a significant decline in idea diversity (Hedges’ g: -0.86) , and a rising consumer 'authenticity premium'. Rather than viewing AI as a human replacement, I propose the Director-Assistant Paradigm. In this symbiotic framework, humans provide the necessary 'entropic disruption' (risk-driven variance) while AI provides 'syntropic refinement' (scalable execution). Ultimately, this work defines the mathematical and biological boundaries required to keep intelligence generative rather than just efficient.

title: Evaluation of cross-cultural communication effectiveness of advertising creative based on adversarial sample robustness test
abstract: With the growing use of deep learning in advertising content generation, model robustness in cross-cultural scenarios has become increasingly critical.Adversarial perturbations can distort ad semantics and undermine communication effectiveness.This study evaluates how such perturbations influence acceptance, emotional resonance, and behavioural responses across cultural groups.We propose an integrated framework combining adversarial robustness testing and cultural adaptation assessment, construct a cross-cultural communication platform, and design adversarial attacks for image and text ads based on real data.Using multidimensional metrics, we compare performance differences across cultural groups.Results show that even mild perturbations induce semantic drift and inconsistent audience responses, while the proposed framework improves communication stability by 42% and restores 91% of cultural adaptability after attacks in Chinese and English user groups.The study offers empirical evidence for the coupled relationship between robustness and cultural context and provides guidance for building resilient advertising generation systems and cross-cultural communication strategies.

title: The Complexity of Dynamic LZ77 is \(\tilde \Theta(n^{2/3})\)
abstract: The Lempel–Ziv 77 (LZ77) factorization is a fundamental compression scheme widely used in text processing and data compression. In this work, we investigate the time complexity of maintaining the LZ77 factorization of a dynamic string. By establishing matching upper and lower bounds, we fully characterize the complexity of this problem.

title: A Post-Quantum Lower Bound for the Distributed Lovasz Local Lemma
abstract: In this work, we study the Lovász local lemma (LLL) problem in the area of distributed quantum computing, which has been the focus of attention of recent advances in quantum computing [STOC’24, STOC’25, STOC’25]. We prove a lower bound of \(2^{\Omega(\log^*n)}\) for the complexity of the distributed LLL in the quantum-LOCAL model. More specifically, we obtain our lower bound already for a very well-studied special case of the LLL, called sinkless orientation, in a stronger model than quantum-LOCAL, called the randomized online-LOCAL model. As a consequence, we obtain the same lower bounds for sinkless orientation and the distributed LLL also in a variety of other models studied across different research communities.

title: Diameter-Constrained Topology Orchestration for Communication-Convergence Tradeoffs in Decentralized Federated Learning
abstract: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) is pivotal for the integration of AI and communication in 6G, facilitating distributed edge-network learning without centralized coordination. However, existing DFL frameworks suffer from prohibitive communication overhead and slow convergence, with a critical issue being the difficulty of balancing the tradeoffs between communication efficiency and convergence rates. This paper proposes a novel distributed synchronization topology orchestration method for DFL that leverages the diameter of the communication graph as a tunable parameter to optimize this communication-convergence tradeoff. Our key insight stems from the relationship between the topology diameter and the spectral radius of the consensus matrix, i.e., constraining the diameter reduces the spectral radius, thereby accelerating convergence while minimizing communication costs. Specifically, we formulate the synchronization topology design as a diameter-constrained minimum spanning tree (MST) problem, where the diameter serves as an adjustable parameter to balance the tradeoff. To ensure robustness in dynamic networks, we further devise a distributed adaptation mechanism that maintains the diameterconstrained MST despite node/link failures. Experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset demonstrate that our method achieves accuracy comparable to fully connected topologies while reducing communication costs by 25% and accelerating convergence by 28% against state-of-the-art benchmarks.

evidence.title: Diameter-Constrained Topology Orchestration for Communication-Convergence Tradeoffs in Decentralized Federated Learning
evidence.abstract: Decentralized federated learning (DFL) is pivotal for the integration of AI and communication in 6G, facilitating distributed edge-network learning without centralized coordination. However, existing DFL frameworks suffer from prohibitive communication overhead and slow convergence, with a critical issue being the difficulty of balancing the tradeoffs between communication efficiency and convergence rates. This paper proposes a novel distributed synchronization topology orchestration method for DFL that leverages the diameter of the communication graph as a tunable parameter to optimize this communication-convergence tradeoff. Our key insight stems from the relationship between the topology diameter and the spectral radius of the consensus matrix, i.e., constraining the diameter reduces the spectral radius, thereby accelerating convergence while minimizing communication costs. Specifically, we formulate the synchronization topology design as a diameter-constrained minimum spanning tree (MST) problem, where the diameter serves as an adjustable parameter to balance the tradeoff. To ensure robustness in dynamic networks, we further devise a distributed adaptation mechanism that maintains the diameterconstrained MST despite node/link failures. Experiments on the CIFAR-10 dataset demonstrate that our method achieves accuracy comparable to fully connected topologies while reducing communication costs by 25% and accelerating convergence by 28% against state-of-the-art benchmarks.

title: HQC 2 NN: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Drone Detection for Low-SNR Conditions in Low-Altitude Economy Networks
abstract: Recently, shortage of ground-based communication, transportation, and surveillance services has prompted the exploration of low-altitude airspace, that leads to Low-altitude economy (LAE) networks. Unlike traditional uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) systems, LAE envisions dense networks of flying platforms that serve both as mobile base stations and service nodes. However, the malicious deployment of UAVs in LAE networks can result in serious disasters. Therefore, robust and real-time UAV threat detection capabilities are required, particularly for low-signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. To address these challenges within LAE networks, we propose a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Convolutional Neural Network (HQC2NN) for low-SNR RF drone signal classification. The model fuses classical feature extraction with quantum variational circuits to leverage quantum superposition and entanglement for improved representation learning.By providing an efficient and noise-resilient RF sensing mechanism, the proposed HQC2NN directly supports the sensing plane of LAE architectures, enabling reliable situational awareness in dense, interference-prone environments. Simulations demonstrate a classification accuracy of 97.3%, outperforming classical counterparts under noisy conditions. The results underscore the potential of quantum-enhanced deep learning models for robust RF signal analysis and real-time drone detection.

title: Multi-Scale Feature and Prompt Learning for Few-Shot Medical Image Anomaly Detection
abstract: Few-shot anomaly detection in medical imaging remains challenging due to the scarcity of labeled abnormal samples and the need for robust feature representations. We propose AnomaMed, a novel multi-scale feature and prompt learning framework that extends Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) for medical anomaly detection. We introduce Prompt Feature Fusion Modules, which integrate multi-scale image and prompt feature fusion at different layers of a pretrained CLIP model, enabling hierarchical feature refinement for improved anomaly localization. Additionally, we incorporate self-attention-based prompt learning, dynamically refining textual representations to enhance text-image alignment in few-shot settings. To further improve generalization, we introduce the Artificial Anomaly Blending Module (AABM), which synthetically generates diverse medical anomalies, enabling the model to learn a broader range of pathological patterns. We evaluate AnomaMed on three benchmark medical imaging datasets, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance over existing vision-language models for few-shot anomaly detection. Results confirm that AnomaMed significantly improves anomaly detection and localization, validating the effectiveness of multi-scale feature fusion, self-attentive prompt learning, and synthetic anomaly augmentation.

title: TILES: Transformer-Based Incremental Learning for Expanding Segmenter
abstract: Incrementally learning new semantic concepts while retaining old knowledge is crucial for several real-world applications. Although the impact of backbone size and architectural choices has been extensively studied in non-incremental computer vision tasks for efficiency concerns, class-incremental semantic segmentation models have predominantly relied on large backbones, without providing alternatives with smaller models. Moreover, existing works use non-comparable backbones, which makes it difficult to isolate the impact of the incremental strategy versus the architectural improvements. In this work, we conduct a fair study across existing class-incremental semantic segmentation approaches, disentangling the incremental mechanism gains from the underlying architectural influence. Besides, we introduce TILES (Transformer-based Incremental Learning for Expanding Segmenter), a novel method that leverages the efficiency of small ViT backbones to provide an alternative solution under strict memory constraints. TILES incrementally expands the architecture, enabling learning new concepts while retaining previously acquired knowledge within a limited memory footprint. To address the challenge of background semantic shift, we employ adaptive losses specific to the incremental branches, balancing old and new information. Moreover, we exploit the confidence gained by the model through training data at each increment to propose an efficient branch merging strategy. TILES represents a compelling first alternative for scenarios with stringent memory and computational limitations. Extensive evaluations on challenging benchmarks demonstrate that using smaller backbones result in a drastic performance drop for the current state-of-the-art method, while TILES succeeds to maintain interesting results proving that it is the very suitable for such scenarios.

title: From Chat to Academia: Calibrating Formality in Low-Resource Languages
abstract: How formal should a sentence sound? The answer is rarely limited to formal or informal. In natural communication, formality changes gradually from casual conversation to professional writing and highly academic prose. However, for many low-resource languages, this continuum of graded stylistic shifts remains largely unmodeled. Turkish, despite its rich stylistic variation, still lacks a systematic framework for capturing such gradual shifts. This study introduces LyreSense, a framework designed to represent the full spectrum of formality in Turkish. We integrate human-written texts with annotation assisted by large language models (LLMs) and controlled synthetic text generation to construct a stylistically diverse corpus. Building on this, we propose a style-intensity–calibrated triplet loss that adapts its margin to differences in formality, enabling embeddings to disentangle subtle stylistic variation independently of semantic content. To train efficiently while preserving model capacity, we apply Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) during fine-tuning. Experiments across four incremental formality classes (informal, neutral, formal, and highly formal) demonstrate that LyreSense achieves Macro-F1 of 0.69. Misclassifications are concentrated between adjacent categories, reflecting the natural continuity of formality, while extreme classes are consistently distinguished. LyreSense is more than a framework for Turkish: it establishes a scalable, language-agnostic pipeline for style-sensitive NLP in low-resource settings. By moving beyond binary style distinctions, it demonstrates how lightweight, efficient models can provide nuanced, human-like style awareness for both research and practical applications.

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Framework for High‐Precision and Efficient Cervical Cancer Detection
abstract: ABSTRACT Cervical cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer‐related mortality among women worldwide, emphasising the need for early and accurate diagnosis. Traditional deep learning approaches for cervical cancer detection often suffer from low accuracy, limited generalisation, and high computational complexity. To overcome these challenges, this study introduces CerviScan‐Net, a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates the Shifted Window Transformer (Swin Transformer), EfficientNet, and bidirectional long short‐term memory (BiLSTM)‐Attention modules for precise and efficient cervical cell classification. The Swin Transformer captures global contextual features, EfficientNet extracts fine‐grained local representations with optimised computational efficiency, and the BiLSTM‐Attention mechanism enhances spatial–semantic learning by focusing on diagnostically significant regions. Interpretability is achieved through a hybrid visualisation strategy combining enhanced gradient‐weighted class activation mapping (Grad‐CAM++; for convolutional layers) and attention rollout (for transformer layers), enabling transparent model predictions. The framework was trained and evaluated on the publicly available SipakMed cervical cell dataset, encompassing five cytological categories – dyskeratotic, koilocytotic, metaplastic, parabasal, and superficial–intermediate cells. Comparative analysis against benchmark models, including ResNet‐50 + LSTM, visual geometry group network (VGG)‐16 + LSTM, Xception (extreme inception network), and DenseNet, demonstrated that CerviScan‐Net achieved superior performance with 98.5% accuracy, 96.3% sensitivity, and 99.2% specificity. These results affirm CerviScan‐Net's robustness, clinical interpretability, and potential as a reliable AI‐assisted diagnostic tool for early detection and screening of cervical cancer.

title: Research on adaptive operation of intelligent robotic arms based on SAC algorithm and hierarchical teaching
abstract: An adaptive operation model for intelligent robotic arms based on the integration of the Soft Actor–Critic (SAC) algorithm and hierarchical teaching is proposed. Building upon the existing reinforcement learning control framework, this model incorporates hierarchical teaching's high-level task decomposition and low-level action optimization mechanisms, establishing a comprehensive system spanning state modeling, reward function design, and policy execution. Experimental validation demonstrates that Hierarchical Demonstration Soft Actor–Critic (HD-SAC) achieves a 94.6% success rate in grasping and assembly tasks—approximately 11% higher than traditional SAC—while reducing energy consumption to 111.8 J and completion time to 16.2 s. Even under perturbed conditions, it maintains a success rate above 85% (with the highest reaching 89.3%) and lowers the collision rate to 4.3%, significantly outperforming baseline methods such as SAC and Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3). The results confirm that this method exhibits superior stability and robustness in complex tasks.

title: Benchmarking Blockchain, Federated Learning, and Quantum Evolutionary Algorithm for Combinatorial Optimization
abstract: Fair benchmarking for decentralized Quantum Computing (QC) against equivalent Federated Learning (FL) methods is essential to evaluate the comparative advantages, limitations, and applicability of these emerging paradigms. However, scalable and practical implementations are needed to address this gap. In this work, we deploy a Quantum-inspired Evolutionary Algorithm (QEA) integrated with Blockchain (BC) methods to enable reliable decentralization. Additionally, we adapt a Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) approach for unsupervised FL. Together, these components form the BloQFeL framework, which implements innovative and adaptable BLOckchain-based Quantum computing and Federated Learning techniques to solve combinatorial optimization problems. The goal of BloQFeL is to benchmark BC-based QEA and SOM algorithms against equivalent FL algorithms. We demonstrate its applicability by simultaneously solving equivalent, randomly generated Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) instances using integrated BC-QEA, FL-SOM, and BC-SOM algorithms. For problem sizes up to 100 cities and 50 optimizer nodes, the results showed significant performance variation among systems. Post-hoc analysis revealed that BC-SOM and FL-SOM significantly outperformed BC-QEA, with BC-SOM offering the most efficient overall performance. Specifically, FL-SOM achieved the lowest CPU Utilization (30.66 ± 21.37%), Latency (0.58 ± 0.23 s), Route Length (5.11&# x 00 D 7; 10 5 ± 4.24&# x 00 D 7; 10 5 ), and Energy Consumption (6.76 ± 3.92 J), while BC-SOM performed best in Memory Utilization (2315.73 ± 7.77 MB) with comparable results on other metrics. In contrast, BC-QEA consistently recorded higher values across all metrics, such as Latency (4.04 ± 3.63 s) and Energy Consumption (169.76 ± 166.53 J), indicating lower efficiency. These results establish BloQFeL as a robust benchmarking framework and a baseline for future research.

title: Exploring the Integration of Differential Privacy in Cybersecurity Analytics: Balancing Data Utility and Privacy in Threat Intelligence
abstract: To resolve the acute problem of privacy protection and guarantee that data can be used in the context of threat intelligence, this paper considers the implementation of Differential Privacy (DP) in cybersecurity analytics. DP, which is a sound mathematical framework, ensures privacy by adding a controlled noise to data outputs and thus avoids sensitive information disclosure even with auxiliary datasets. The use of DP in Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems is highlighted, and it can be seen that DP has the capability to protect event log and threat data analysis without interfering with the analytical efficiency. The utility versus privacy trade-offs linked to the maximization of the epsilon parameter, which is one of the critical components of DP mechanisms, is pointed out. The article shows the transformative power of DP in promoting safe sharing of data and joint threat intelligence through real-world systems and case studies. Finally, this paper makes DP one of the key strategies to improve privacy-preserving analytics in the field of cybersecurity.

title: Joint Optimization of Speaker and Spoof Detectors for Spoofing-Robust Automatic Speaker Verification
abstract: Spoofing-robust speaker verification (SASV) combines the tasks of speaker and spoof detection to authenticate speakers under adversarial settings. Many SASV systems rely on fusion of speaker and spoof cues at embedding, score or decision levels, based on independently trained subsystems. In this study, we respect similar modularity of the two subsystems, by integrating their outputs using trainable back-end classifiers. In particular, we explore various approaches for directly optimizing the back-end for the recently-proposed SASV performance metric (a-DCF) as a training objective. Our experiments on the ASVspoof 5 dataset demonstrate two important findings: (i) nonlinear score fusion consistently improves a-DCF over linear fusion, and (ii) the combination of weighted cosine scoring for speaker detection with SSL-AASIST for spoof detection achieves state-of-the-art performance, reducing min a-DCF to 0.196 and SPF-EER to 7.6%. These contributions highlight the importance of modular design, calibrated integration, and task-aligned optimization for advancing robust and interpretable SASV systems.

title: Piecemaker: A Resource-Efficient Entanglement Distribution Protocol
abstract: We introduce multipartite entanglement distribution protocols that use a quantum switch to deliver stabilizer states to a number of remote end users. As in existing schemes, the first step in our protocols involves Bell pair generation between the switch and each end user. However, unlike existing schemes that wait for all Bell pairs to be established before distributing the desired state -- for example, via a projective measurement -- our approach stores only a minimal subset of Bell pairs while processing every subsequent Bell pair immediately. In doing so, our protocols reduce the average Bell pair storage time compared to existing schemes, resulting in less cumulative noise as a direct consequence. title: Quantum-classical hybrid computation of electron transfer in a cryptochrome protein via VQE-PDFT and multiscale modeling
abstract: a noiseless quantum circuit simulator, on the charge-transfer dataset confirmed that VQE-PDFT achieved results comparable to conventional MC-PDFT. Building upon this, we developed shallow-depth hardware-efficient ansatz circuits and integrated them into a QM/MM multiscale architecture to enable applications in complex biological systems. This extended framework, when applied to electron transfer in the European robin cryptochrome protein ErCRY4 with noiseless simulations, yielded transfer rates that aligned well with experimental measurements. Finally, as a proof-of-concept hardware demonstration, we executed reduced-density-matrix measurements for a single protein conformation on a 13-qubit superconducting device and showed the impact of noise through a comprehensive error analysis.

title: M3S-UPD: Efficient Multi-Stage Self-Supervised Learning for Fine-Grained Encrypted Traffic Classification With Unknown Pattern Discovery
abstract: The growing complexity of encrypted network traffic presents dual challenges for modern network management: accurate multiclass classification of known applications and reliable detection of unknown traffic patterns. Although deep learning models show promise in controlled environments, their real-world deployment is hindered by data scarcity, concept drift, and operational constraints. This paper proposes M3S-UPD, a novel Multi-Stage Self-Supervised Unknown-aware Packet Detection framework that synergistically integrates semi-supervised learning with representation analysis. Our approach eliminates artificial segregation between classification and detection tasks through a four-phase iterative process: 1) probabilistic embedding generation, 2) clustering-based structure discovery, 3) distribution-aligned outlier identification, and 4) confidence-aware model updating. Key innovations include a self-supervised unknown detection mechanism that requires neither synthetic samples nor prior knowledge, and a continuous learning architecture that is resistant to performance degradation. Experimental results show that M3S-UPD not only outperforms existing methods on the few-shot encrypted traffic classification task, but also simultaneously achieves competitive performance on the zero-shot unknown traffic discovery task.

title: KNN Short-term Photovoltaic Power Prediction Algorithm Based on Interval Division
abstract: To enhance the dispatchability of photovoltaic power generation and improve equipment status observability, this study investigates short-term PV power forecasting. By collecting environmental parameters to construct datasets and analyzing existing prediction methods, we propose an improved K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) prediction model. The model introduces an interval partitioning mechanism that determines output intervals based on real-time samples' proximity to historical data in feature space. It then performs weighted calculations using the K closest historical sample power values within each interval to generate final predictions. This approach features a simple structure and high computational efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the model achieves an average absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 7.83% and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.5053, with precision meeting engineering application requirements. These findings provide effective technical support for intelligent operation of photovoltaic power stations.

title: PERAMALAN INTENSITAS RADIASI MATAHARI KOTA PEKANBARU MENGGUNAKAN JARINGAN SYARAF TIRUAN PROPAGASI BALIK
abstract: Kota Pekanbaru memiliki potensi radiasi matahari yang tinggi sebagai wilayah tropis untuk pengembangan Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Surya (PLTS), apabila didukung oleh data radiasi matahari yang akurat. Pengembangan PLTS tidak hanya memerlukan data historis, tetapi juga peramalan radiasi matahari di masa mendatang untuk mendukung optimalisasi sistem PLTS serta perhitungan kelayakan finansial. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan model peramalan intensitas radiasi matahari untuk periode enam tahun ke depan menggunakan Jaringan Syaraf Tiruan (JST) dengan algoritma backpropagation, melalui pengombinasian jumlah neuron pada hidden layer dan nilai learning rate guna memperoleh performa pelatihan terbaik. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa model dengan arsitektur 5–20–1 dan learning rate 0,01 memberikan kinerja optimal, dengan nilai MSE sebesar 0,013076, MAPE 1,97%, dan R² 0,898 pada tahap pelatihan, serta MSE 0,0307, MAPE 2,71%, dan R² 0,7657 pada tahap pengujian. Hasil peramalan periode 2025–2030 menunjukkan intensitas radiasi matahari berada pada kisaran 4,2–5,2 kWh/m²/hari dengan rata-rata tahunan sebesar 4,7 kWh/m²/hari, yang mengikuti pola musiman secara konsisten. Hasil penelitian ini diharapkan dapat menyediakan metode dan informasi peramalan yang mendukung perencanaan serta pengembangan PLTS di Kota Pekanbaru.

title: THE ROLE OF AI-POWERED CHATBOTS IN IMPROVING CUSTOMER SATISFACTION ON E-COMMERCE PLATFORMS
abstract: In today’s highly competitive and digitally driven marketplace, e-commerce businesses are increasingly leveraging Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies to optimize operations and promote customer experiences. As part of these technologies, AI-powered Chatbots have become a prominent tool for enhancing customer satisfaction by delivering instant, accurate, and personalized responses. Through the review of recent literature and real-world case studies, this paper assessed the role of AI-powered Chatbots in improving customer satisfaction on e-commerce platforms by highlighting how they enhance personalization and customer engagement, provide 24/7 availability and instant support, handle repetitive queries and reduce telephone cost, offer accuracy, accessibility, and reliability, and promote faster resolution and scalability. This study also explores AI-powered Chatbots challenges encountered by users on e-commerce platforms. The study concludes that e-commerce businesses utilizing AI-powered Chatbots can improve customer satisfaction, trust, and loyalty while also gaining competitive edge and customer retention. Hence, this study recommends that as AI-powered Chatbots become increasingly prevalent in e-commerce, businesses must continually enhance their technology to improve Chatbot-human interactions, and promote long-term brand loyalty through continuous innovation.

title: Fig.3 of the main text.
abstract: In quantum networks, after passing through noisy channels or information processing, residual states may lack sufficient entanglement for further tasks, yet they may retain hidden quantum resources that can be recycled. Efficiently recycling these states to extract entanglement resources such as genuine multipartite entanglement or Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen pairs is essential for optimizing network performance. Here, we develop a tripartite entanglement distillation scheme using an eight-photon quantum platform, demonstrating entanglement superactivation phenomena which are unique to multipartite systems. We successfully generate a three-photon genuinely entangled state from two bi-separable states via local operations and classical communication, demonstrating superactivation of genuine multipartite entanglement.Furthermore, we extend our scheme to generate a three-photon state capable of extracting an Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen pair from two initial states lacking this capability, revealing a previously unobserved entanglement superactivation phenomenon. Our methods and findings offer not only practical applications for quantum networks, but also lead to a deeper understanding of multipartite entanglement structures.

title: The Model State Attestation Framework: Evidence-Based Governance for Foundation Models
abstract: Foundation models now occupy positions of consequential authority across credit adjudication, clinical diagnostics, public resource allocation, and autonomous trading. Yet no unified system exists to cryptographically prove that a specific inference was generated by a verified model version operating in a compliant internal state. Current governance artifacts—model cards, training logs, static benchmarks—are descriptive, self-reported, and fundamentally non-verifiable. This paper proposes the Model State Attestation Framework (MSAF), a three-tier architecture composing hardware-rooted trust (TEE platform attestation), signed continuous internal invariant monitoring (gradient integrity, entropy floor, structural coherence, Lyapunov stability, distributional drift), and periodic deep verification anchors (zkML inference proofs, provenance hashing, contamination detection). A survey of 200+ papers (2022–2026) confirms that while each component exists individually, no system yet composes them into a unified attestation artifact for foundation-scale models. The framework maps composed artifacts to specific evidence requirements across five regulatory domains: EU AI Act (zero harmonized standards published as of February 2026), FDA SaMD (PCCP framework), Federal Reserve SR 11-7, US Federal Procurement (M-26-04), and AI Insurance (projected $4.8B market by 2032). Theoretical ceilings are documented honestly: Rice's theorem bounds the gap between process attestation and behavioral guarantees, the Impossibility Sandwich constrains formal verification of useful models, and TEE physical side-channel attacks (TEE.Fail, HyperTheft, CVE-2024-56161) limit hardware trust assumptions. The honest framing: MSAF provides probabilistic risk reduction and accountability infrastructure—analogous to financial auditing, medical device regulation, and food safety inspection—not behavioral safety guarantees. The building blocks exist, the regulatory pull is strong, and the standards window is open.

title: Cyclic Distinction–Integration Learning via Linear Coherence Bottlenecks
abstract: This paper introduces a cyclic learning framework in which representational enrichment arises through alternating phases of distinction and integration constrained by a linear coherence bottleneck. The model formalizes learning as a stability–plasticity process operating under bandwidth limitations, yielding predictable enrichment per cycle and an analytically tractable optimal period.The framework is presented conservatively as a representation-level learning mechanism, independent of specific biological or cognitive interpretations. Connections to dimensionality control, compression–decompression dynamics, and training stability in artificial learning systems are discussed.This work is exploratory and theoretical in nature and is intended to support further empirical investigation and ablation in machine learning and related domains.

title: 完全验证的有理数域与约分系统：基于Coq的形
abstract: The main innovations of this work include:A Fully Verified Rational Reduction System: It is the first to simultaneously verify functional correctness, performance guarantees (e.g., strict decrease of numerator/denominator), and algebraic compatibility within a formal environment.Setoid Field Theory: A novel field construction method based on equivalence relations is proposed, which simplifies the proof process and reduces the proof code volume by approximately 37%.A Hierarchical Algebra Library: It supports type-safe construction from semigroups to fields, offering excellent extensibility and engineering practicality.Cross-Domain Application Validation: The potential of the library has been demonstrated in cryptography (RSA modular inverse), quantum computing (phase estimation), and scientific computing (fluid dynamics discretization).All code has been open-sourced on GitHub and supports extraction to executable code in languages like OCaml and C++, providing a reusable formal foundation for building highly reliable numerical computation systems. This research advances formal verification from theory to engineering practice, laying the groundwork for trustworthy computing in critical fields such as cryptography, quantum computing, and artificial intelligence. 本工作的主要创新包括： 完全验证的约分系统：首次在形式化环境中同时验证功能正确性、性能保证与代数相容性； Setoid 域理论：提出基于等价关系的域构造方法，简化证明流程，减少约 37% 的证明代码量; 层次化代数库：支持从半群到域的类型安全构造，具备良好的可扩展性与工程实用性； 跨领域应用验证：已在密码学（RSA 模逆元）、量子计算（相位估计）与科学计算（流体力学离散化）中展示应用潜力。 所有代码已在 GitHub 开源，支持提取为 OCaml/C++ 等执行代码，为构建高可靠数值计算系统提供了可复用的形式化基础。本研究推动了形式化验证从理论走向工程实践，为密码学、量子计算、人工智能等关键领域的可信计算奠定了基础。

title: Designing for Student Engagement with AI in Courseware: Lessons from Iterative Improvements to DOT in REAL CHEM
abstract: This design-based research study reports on a Learning Engineering (LE) cycle embedded within the broader REAL CHEM courseware initiative, examining how students use and perceive DOT, a generative AI tutor for general chemistry. In Fall 2024, student awareness and engagement with DOT were low, and interviews revealed reliance on external AI tools and limited generative use. Guided by LE principles—human-centered design, iterative refinement, and evidence-informed decision making—we redesigned DOT by refining its base prompt and introducing AI Activation Points to make the system more proactive and contextually aligned with student workflows. Summer 2025 findings showed increased awareness, higher engagement, and improved student satisfaction. Results illustrate how targeted, iterative LE cycles can improve the effectiveness of AI-enabled learning supports at scale.

title: Integrated Disaster Situation Management System with Domain-Specific Ontology Model
abstract: Disaster response and management in the era of climate change require seamless coordination across numerous agencies, systems, and stakeholders. A shared understanding of the situation is critical as responders from different organizations (e.g., fire, medical, military) must work in concert under high pressure. The common ontological definition is important for various stakeholders and expert groups to understand disaster during its different stages for controlling and managing salvation and recovery. Semantic interoperability works in practice between different organizations by creating a common language and meaning structure that enables information to be exchanged and understood without misunderstanding. This is achieved through a common ontology that defines key concepts unambiguously. This research examines the creation of common ontology and semantics aspects during nature disaster identification and management. In this study the MobiJOPA™ has been the use case environment system. It was created recently by the Start-up company Husqtec Corp., which is concentrating on situation and operational management. Use case has been a water flow disaster, which is a quite common type of disaster due to the influence of climate change. During the research has been answered to the following research questions: •How is the integrated situation awareness system dynamics structured and organized?•How is system functioning and human interoperability organized by the ontology interface?•How is data, information, and knowledge economy structured and managed?•How is stakeholder training organized, and knowledge gathered to create an ontology interface, routing common disaster understanding?Semantic infrastructure supports information integration by combining heterogeneous data sources, such as sensors and social media, into a unified information model. Semantic interoperability is not an abstract benefit; it operationalizes the data in ways that closely support the real tasks and decisions of emergency management. It creates a common operating environment where each piece of information is readily available to those who need it, in a form they can understand and trust. It moves the focus from low-level data wrangling to higher-level analysis and action. Building such interoperability requires understanding the real-world semantics, linking formal data to meanings that make sense to humans in their roles. In other words, the ontology must be grounded in the language and practice of emergency responders. This ensures that technology aligns with human thinking, further enhancing clarity and coordination. Semantic interoperability enabled by a common ontology and robust system architecture provides shared situational awareness and efficient coordination in disaster management. It reduces information fragmentation and miscommunication.

It creates a common operating environment where each piece of information is readily available to those who need it, in a form they can understand and trust. It moves the focus from low-level data wrangling to higher-level analysis and action. Building such interoperability requires understanding the real-world semantics, linking formal data to meanings that make sense to humans in their roles. In other words, the ontology must be grounded in the language and practice of emergency responders. This ensures that technology aligns with human thinking, further enhancing clarity and coordination. Semantic interoperability enabled by a common ontology and robust system architecture provides shared situational awareness and efficient coordination in disaster management. It reduces information fragmentation and miscommunication.

title: Artificial Intelligence In Aviation And Aerospace
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is quickly changing aerospace, fields traditionally shaped by human creativity and engineering skill. AI helps optimize rocket trajectories and allows for autonomous spacecraft navigation. It has become a crucial part of modern exploration. Its capacity to handle large amounts of data in real time enables engineers to foresee mechanical failures before they happen. It also helps design more efficient propulsion systems and simulate complex missions to distant planets. It can also pre-calculate whether our expectations from an aircraft are met as per design conjectures. As humanity aims to colonize Mars and expand the limits of space travel, AI serves as both a driving force and a protector. It is transforming how we build, launch, and maintain the machines that help us to circumnavigate and go beyond the Earth. The objective of this hybrid review is to find and abstractly define AI's use in aviation. analyze faults that can occur due to its use from real published fault reports and extrapolate its use in Aeronautics and in some cases Astronautics. All inferences are concluded based on exhaustive review of research by reports published by credible government recognized sources on events occurring from the date of induction of AI in the field of aerospace. Multiple angles were viewed mostly from the consumer, the manufacturer and regular civilians.

title: Securing the AI Supply Chain: Safeguarding U.S. Advantage in the Age of Generative AI
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) now supports nearly every domain of national power, from intelligence fusion and logistics to cyber defense and information operations. Unlike traditional defense systems, AI depends on a globally distributed supply chain spanning data, models, and compute. Other critical systems also rely on global supply chains, but AI is distinctive in its dependence on large-scale data, open-source software, and foreign-fabricated chips, each of which introduces distinct avenues for compromise. The AI supply chain includes every stage of an algorithm’s lifecycle: data ingestion, labeling, model training, deployment, and post-deployment monitoring. Because these processes draw on open-source tools, commercial cloud services, and foreign-made chips, assurance gaps now extend across the entire stack. Recent incidents highlight how these risks have shifted inside modern AI ecosystems. In 2024, researchers discovered malicious model payloads on open-source platforms such as Hugging Face and prompt-injection exploits targeting GitHub Copilot, demonstrating that compromise can begin with poisoned data or manipulated model weights, not just zero-day exploits. The United States therefore faces a dual imperative: to preserve the openness that drives innovation while hardening the AI supply chain against adversarial manipulation. Achieving this balance requires an ecosystem that is verifiable, governable, and resilient.

abstract: Le texte analyse les inférences, en particulier les inférences des constructions polylexicales, notamment des verbes supports. En vue de l’amélioration de la capacité des systèmes automatisés à gérer les inférences, une approche systématique pour décrire la signature implicative des verbes supports et des verbes « pleins » est proposée.

title: Performance Analysis of Groth16 zkSNARK: Systematic Benchmarking with Circom-snarkjs
abstract: Zero-knowledge succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge (zk-SNARKs) have emerged as a critical technology for privacy-preserving computation and blockchain applications. However, systematic performance analysis of practical implementations remains limited, hindering informed technology adoption decisions. This study presents a comprehensive benchmarking analysis of the Groth16 protocol implementation using the widely-adopted Circom-snarkjs framework. We developed an automated benchmarking platform that systematically measures performance across seven representative circuit types with varying computational complexity (1-11 R1CS constraints). Our methodology ensures reproducible measurements through controlled experimental design with statistical validation. The platform captures detailed metrics for all three phases of the Groth16 protocol: witness generation, proof creation, and verification. Results from 35 independent measurements reveal several important findings. Witness generation demonstrates consistent performance across circuit types, averaging 57.6±12.1 milliseconds. Proof generation times range from 832 to 1,147 milliseconds, showing non-linear scaling with circuit complexity. Verification times remain relatively stable (741-884 milliseconds), confirming Groth16's theoretical constant-time verification advantage. All measurements achieved 100% success rate with complete proof validation. Notably, circuit structure significantly impacts performance beyond simple constraint counting. Comparison-based circuits achieve 13.22 constraints per second efficiency, substantially outperforming arithmetic circuits (1.02-4.36 constraints/second). This finding provides actionable guidance for circuit design optimization. The study contributes an open-source benchmarking framework for reproducible zk-SNARK research and provides empirical performance data for technology adoption decisions. Our findings support the practical deployment of Groth16 for applications requiring efficient zero-knowledge proofs while highlighting optimization opportunities for circuit designers.

title: Towards LLM-Informed Topic Modeling
abstract: Topic modeling automatically discovers themes in large collections of text. Early probabilistic models built the foundation, and newer neural models improved flexibility with deep learning. Yet, challenges remain in clarity, evaluation, and adapting to different kinds of text. This thesis combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with neural topic models to address these issues. It introduces methods that make text collections easier to interpret, improve how quality is measured, and strengthen the ability to apply models across domains. The findings show that combining topic models with LLMs creates clearer, more reliable, and more adaptable tools for understanding text.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning optimization with Connection Pruning Techniques
abstract: It helps optimizing Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) by providing data* on the effect of implementing connection pruning techniques. *It provides example data on how the model behaves. Since DRL tasks are randomized, the behavioral patterns of the model are likely to be similar when implementing pruning techniques compared to when none are used. *added new code 2026 January 2026 Update on A2C Connection Pruning Experiments After discussions with fellow practitioners, it was requested to introduce an alternative method to mimic connection pruning. Instead of relying on increasing dropout rates to simulate temporarily disabling connections during training, the current update implements a soft reset, where the lowest-magnitude weights are explicitly set to zero. This approach provides a more controlled and interpretable form of connection pruning while maintaining network stability. After extensive discussion and review, this update introduces a more explicit and controlled form of connection pruning: Forced Progressive Connection Pruning After each N actions, a fixed fraction of the lowest-magnitude weights in the network are set to zero (effective reset). A safety limit ensures that at least 50% of connections remain in every layer, preventing catastrophic network failure. This implements true, pruning (effective reset) rather than the temporary stochastic masking of dropout. By removing the weakest weights, the network gradually emphasizes the most important connections, reducing redundancy. Progressive pruning applied after each N actions ensures stability while the agent learns. cc: martinkaloev2023@gmail.com

title: Design and Construction of a Mobile Robot for the URC and ERC Competitions
abstract: Abstract. This article presents the components of a mobile robot prepared for the international URC and ERC "Mars rovers" competitions. The URC and ERC competitions are the largest robotics and space events, targeting the worlds of science and business, the new technologies sector, and the general public. The European Rover Challenge, like the University Rover Challenge, is part of the Rover Challenge Series – a league of the most prestigious competitions for robotic mobile vehicles. The core of the competition is the international Mars robot competition, which attracts students, graduates, and academics from universities around the world. Teams of around a dozen people work for twelve months to develop a fully functional, next-generation Mars rover. Each team includes specialists in mechatronics, automation, robotics, autonomy, communications, and navigation.

title: Curvature as a Measure of Interpretive Load
abstract: This registration documents Curvature as a Measure of Interpretive Load, a structural analysis of how accumulated coherence compresses semantic space and increases the effort required to introduce, sustain, or revise distinctions within meaning-bearing systems. The work introduces semantic curvature as a relational measure for describing interpretive load, rather than as a numerical metric, operational indicator, or optimization target. The analysis reframes stability and coherence as conditions that carry structural cost. As interpretations, categories, and representations accumulate, semantic space deforms, producing curvature that reshapes interpretive movement. In highly curved environments, some interpretations become easy and natural to sustain, while others encounter steep resistance regardless of their logical validity or relevance. Interpretive difficulty is thus treated as a function of structural compression rather than complexity, disagreement, or bias. This project distinguishes curvature from bias, distortion, or ideological skew. Curvature is defined as a content-independent structural condition that favors continuity and stability over deviation and revision. A system may exhibit extreme curvature even under conditions of technical accuracy, procedural correctness, or normative neutrality. Curvature explains how systems can appear coherent, aligned, and mature while becoming increasingly resistant to alternative interpretation. The registration situates curvature as a foundational mechanism within the broader structural ecology articulated in earlier registrations. Rising curvature is shown to produce premature coherence by compressing semantic space before exploration is complete, and to contribute to irreversibility by raising the cost of reopening collapsed distinctions beyond reconstructive capacity. Semantic propagation follows curvature gradients, while boundary failure and proxy substitution further intensify compression. Particular attention is given to AI-mediated environments, where representational persistence, probabilistic smoothing, and reinforcement mechanisms accelerate curvature accumulation. In such systems, coherence is not merely reflected but actively stabilized, shifting interpretive load from human judgment to structural constraint. Meaning becomes easier to reproduce and increasingly costly to revise. The analysis is intentionally non-prescriptive. No curvature metrics, computational measures, governance thresholds, or optimization strategies are proposed. Curvature is presented as a condition to be recognized rather than a parameter to be managed. The purpose of this registration is conceptual and structural: to clarify how interpretive load emerges from accumulation and why stability is often misinterpreted as neutrality or resolution. This description reflects an open-ended theoretical articulation rather than a finalized framework. The concepts documented here establish semantic curvature as a non-quantitative structural measure that may inform future analytical, empirical, or applied work within the Meta-Writing Ecology. title: Fusion technique for handling imbalanced and overlapped dataset to improve the performance of existing classifiers
abstract: The effectiveness of the classifier in efficiently classifying the data is diminished by imbalanced class data. Employing a supervised method to address imbalanced data may result in the exclusion of majority classes. The overlap of class instances can complicate the learning process of the classifier. In this paper, three different algorithms were proposed to handle the imbalance problem. The proposed algorithms MCROR, RbImbD and Fused-MCRb with different working mechanisms were applied to balance the majority and the minority classes present in the given dataset. Twenty-three publicly available dataset and 12 synthesised dataset were used to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithms. The results were calculated on different performance metrices: precision, sensitivity, F1 score and geometric mean. The values obtained for different metrices shows that the proposed algorithms significantly improved the performance of the classifier and handle the imbalance classes in the given dataset.

title: Casper: A Causality-Inspired Defense With Confounder Against Label Inference Attacks in Vertical Split Federated Learning
abstract: Vertical Split Federated Learning (VSFL) allows participants to collaboratively train a better model with different features vertically partitioned in the same sample space, where the model is divided into bottom model and top model by the cut layer, trained by passive and active participants respectively. However, in the process, the labels owned by the active participant will still be inferred or stolen by curious or malicious passive participants. In this paper, we propose Casper, a causality-inspired defense mechanism with a confounder against label inference attacks in VSFL. Casper first analyzes the feasibility of optimizing the training process in VSFL at the intervention level from a causal perspective. It then introduces a confounder consisting of cut layer output reconstruction and label obfuscation to disrupt the direct causality between cut layer outputs and labels. Additionally, we integrate selective discrepancy training to further ensure model utility by strategically balancing training between active and passive participants. Extensive experiments conducted on four datasets across different tasks demonstrate that Casper effectively preserves label privacy while maintaining model performance, significantly outperforming current advanced defending methods in VSFL.

title: An Efficient Radial Basis Function Neural Network With Hybrid Regularizations for Predicting Library Loan Volume: Generalization and Adaptability Are Improved
abstract: Radial basis function neural networks (RBFNNs) have been widely used in data modeling and prediction in recent years. However, an RBFNN does not perform well when it comes to practical problems, such as library loan volume prediction. This happens mainly because the existing RBFNNs overly focus on minimizing training errors, which leads to overfitting and uneven distributions of parameters. In particular, uneven distributions of parameters result in a failure of the RBFNN to cover the dynamic characteristics of the library loan volume. To solve this problem, this article proposes an efficient RBFNN with hybrid regularizations (RBF-HR) for predicting the library loan volume. In the proposed RBF-HR, we design an efficient dynamic repulsion regularization (DRR) of center and adaptive regularization of width to improve the generalization and adaptability for practical problems. We also verify the effectiveness of the proposed RBF-HR in predicting the library loan volume.

evidence.title: An Efficient Radial Basis Function Neural Network With Hybrid Regularizations for Predicting Library Loan Volume: Generalization and Adaptability Are Improved
evidence.abstract: Radial basis function neural networks (RBFNNs) have been widely used in data modeling and prediction in recent years. However, an RBFNN does not perform well when it comes to practical problems, such as library loan volume prediction. This happens mainly because the existing RBFNNs overly focus on minimizing training errors, which leads to overfitting and uneven distributions of parameters. In particular, uneven distributions of parameters result in a failure of the RBFNN to cover the dynamic characteristics of the library loan volume. To solve this problem, this article proposes an efficient RBFNN with hybrid regularizations (RBF-HR) for predicting the library loan volume. In the proposed RBF-HR, we design an efficient dynamic repulsion regularization (DRR) of center and adaptive regularization of width to improve the generalization and adaptability for practical problems. We also verify the effectiveness of the proposed RBF-HR in predicting the library loan volume.

title: FedMeanStd: Federated Aggregation With Outliers Filtering
abstract: Federated Learning faces significant challenges due to data heterogeneity, particularly in non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) environments. This issue hampers the accuracy and convergence of traditional aggregation methods like Federated Averaging (FedAvg). To overcome this problem, this study proposes FedMeanStd, a novel aggregation technique utilizing the mean and standard deviation of client updates to dynamically select participants. This selection ensures that only stable, relevant contributions are included in the global model, filtering out unreliable or extreme updates. FedMeanStd introduces a statistically driven filtering mechanism that improves robustness against outliers and enhances the consistency of client selection. It operates entirely at the server side, preserving client privacy and scalability. Evaluated on benchmark datasets including CIFAR-10 and FashionMNIST under extreme non-IID settings, FedMeanStd consistently achieves superior accuracy and stability compared to traditional methods such as FedAvg, FedAvgM, and FedProx. By leveraging statistical measures, the method promotes balanced and representative learning, resulting in a more robust global model.

title: Benign-Malignant Breast Histology Classification using MobileNet Variants: An Analysis
abstract: Automatic analysis of the medical data is one of the common practices followed to detect diseases with better accuracy. Deep Learning (DL) tool-based medical image examination is one of the approved clinical practices, and the outcome of this process supports the treatment planning and execution. This work proposes a DL tool based on the ConvNeXt (CN) scheme to classify the chosen Breast Histology Images (BHI) into benign and malignant classes. The various phases of the proposed DL-tool include: image collection from the database and resizing it to 224x224x3 pixels, feature extraction using the chosen CN-model, feature reduction using 50% dropout, and serial features fusion to get fused- features-vector (FFV), and binary classification with 5-fold cross-validation. The merit of the developed scheme is confirmed using the classification executed with the chosen CN-feature and the FFV. The outcome of this study confirms that the FFV-based classification provides a detection result upto 99% when the SoftMax-based classification is executed. This confirms that the proposed DL-tool provides a better result on the chosen image database.
